newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares ended sharply weaker on Tuesday in line with bourses around Europe, sent into decline by news of a retalitory U.S. missile strike on Iraq.
The Dutch AEX index of leading shares closed 4.00 points lower at 550.98, well off an earlier low of 546.70.

The market started under pressure as news of the attack was digested, hitting bonds and stocks alike. Increased nervousness of an impending rise in U.S. interest rates after recent strong economic data was also weighing on the market.
But a rally in the oil price fed through into demand for oil stocks, making Royal Dutch the star performer in Amsterdam.
For much of the day Royal Dutch was only stock in positive territory and although for short time it too dipped into the red, the oil giant climbed to close 0.90 guilders up at 252.80.

But nearly all other stocks ended in negative territory, with banks ING and ABN AMRO both attracting relatively heavy trade and sustaining sharp losses. With little other fundamental news, financials are seen as one of the most vulnerable sectors when the whole index comes under pressure.
But dealers said there was little aggressive short selling around and pegged the fall more to a lack of investor buying and option-related selling, characterised by increased volatility.
ING was the most active, finishing 0.80 guilders lower at 51.20. ABN AMRO was 1.20 down at 89.70 guilders.
"The only major sellers today have been the option holders, thy've had to readjust their portfolios," one dealer said.

But dealers said the picture was not too negative and drew some comfort from today's U.S. economic data -- the August National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index, which they said may have calmed some rate rise fears.
Bund futures and Dutch bonds rallied on the figures providing some support for the stock market, which also saw some of its strong dollar-related prop erode in the afternoon.
News on the corporate front was realtively quiet today, with early release of first half figures from Cap Volmac and bourse debutant Van Leer, which both posted sharply higher net results.
Despite this, Cap Volmac ended 1.00 guilder down at 36.50 and Van Leer unchanged at 32.90 guilders, undermined by the general weak tone of the market.

But the AEX's close back above 550 points left the index in relatively good shape, dealers said, adding buying opportunities were still being presented on the lows although it still faced significant chart resistance above 560 points.
